data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["A compiler executes steps without judgment; panel members must interpret checklist items, introducing judgment variance absent from compilation.","Compiler correctness is deterministic and reproducible; panel judgments are stochastic and session-dependent.","The expert's intuition has no compiler analog\u2014this would correspond to a hand-written assembly program that outperforms the compiled version in specific cases."],"overturn_conditions":["It is shown that no semantically-equivalent rephrasing test can distinguish genuine understanding from compliance, because all rephrasings inevitably change the task framing.","Empirical evidence shows expert intuition already captures the decision rule implicitly, making the externalization step redundant rather than causally necessary.","The Condorcet independence assumption is violated in all realistic panel settings, eliminating the aggregation benefit."],"shared_structure":["Both checklist-panel and compiled-program involve translating a holistic judgment into discrete verifiable steps.","Both aggregate independent evaluations (panel votes / compiler passes) to suppress random error.","Both risk 'cargo-culting' surface features without understanding the underlying decision rule."],"source_memory_refs":["ba687c5f145e404c53a84549cf366e0b6e0106eec67404c07231357fed09e672"],"transfer_claims":["If panel accuracy survives semantic-equivalent rephrasings of the checklist (analogous to compiler-optimization-invariance), the panel has extracted the decision rule, indicating genuine gain.","If panel accuracy drops under rephrasing, the panel was pattern-matching surface syntax\u2014analogous to overfit code that breaks under refactoring\u2014indicating mere compliance."]},"claim":"A panel of trained non-experts using an explicit checklist will, on average, produce more reliable judgments than a single domain expert using intuition for objectively verifiable outcomes, but only when the task decomposition maps perfectly onto verifiable sub-outcomes; if the checklist forces premature closure on ambiguous indicators, the panel's reliability will equal or fall below the expert's, and genuine gain is distinguishable from mere compliance by checking whether panel accuracy survives perturbations to checklist phrasing that preserve semantic content.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The domain expert's intuition incorporates tacit knowledge that the checklist cannot capture, and this tacit component is causally responsible for correct judgment in >50% of cases.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The task's verifiable outcome is contingent on a latent variable that the checklist does not measure but the expert perceives holistically, so checklist compliance systematically misses edge cases.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The panel's deliberation introduces social-loafing or groupthink dynamics that collapse the independence assumption required for Condorcet-style error suppression.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist is underspecified for boundary cases, and panel majority converges on a wrong but defensible literal reading, whereas the expert's intuition would correctly extrapolate.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"An explicit checklist externalizes the reasoning chain into discrete, independently-verifiable steps. A panel of non-experts provides orthogonal error-correction via majority aggregation (Condorcet jury theorem dynamics), while the checklist ensures each voter applies the same decision criterion rather than relying on heterogeneous intuitions. The causal reliability gain arises from the interaction: the checklist suppresses individual variance, and the panel suppresses residual systematic bias. Genuine gain (vs. mere compliance) is identified by a perturbation test: if panel accuracy is unchanged by semantically-equivalent rephrasings of the checklist, the panel is extracting the underlying decision rule. If accuracy drops, the panel was pattern-matching surface syntax of the checklist without understanding\u2014mere compliance that tracks the answer only under the original phrasing.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
